evidence.snippet: Exposure of mesothelial cells to TGF-β1 increased production of lactate (P < .05), increased HIF1A mRNA (P < .05), and protein, and increased concentrations of mRNAs encoded by glycolysis-associated genes (LDHA, PDK1, SLC2A1; P < .05).
evidence.explanation: TGF-beta1 drives the glycolytic, lactate-secreting phenotype in human peritoneal mesothelial cells, linking peritoneal TGF-beta to the Warburg-like shift.

evidence.snippet: human peritoneal mesothelial cells (HPMCs) recovered from the pelvic peritoneum of women with endometriosis exhibit significantly higher glycolysis, lower mitochondrial respiration, decreased enzymatic activity of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH), and increased production of lactate compared to HPMCs from women without disease
evidence.explanation: Primary mesothelial cells from women with endometriosis show the full Warburg-like signature (higher glycolysis, lower respiration, reduced PDH, more lactate) relative to disease-free controls.

steps/7.description: Endometriotic lesions and the peritoneal mesothelium of women with endometriosis undergo a cancer-like ("Warburg") metabolic shift away from mitochondrial respiration toward aerobic glycolysis. TGF-beta1, which is elevated in endometriosis peritoneal fluid, drives human peritoneal mesothelial cells to upregulate glycolysis-associated genes (HIF1A, PDK1, LDHA, SLC2A1) and secrete lactate. This glycolytic phenotype — higher glycolysis, lower mitochondrial respiration, and reduced pyruvate dehydrogenase activity — favors lesion establishment and survival and is the target of the investigational metabolic therapy dichloroacetate.

evidence.snippet: Estrogen is the most important known factor that stimulates the growth of endometriosis. Estrogen delivery to endometriotic implants was classically viewed to be only via the circulating blood in an endocrine fashion. We recently uncovered an autocrine positive feedback mechanism, which favored the continuous production of estrogen and prostaglandin (PG)E2 in the endometriotic stromal cells.
evidence.explanation: Estrogen drives endometriosis growth through both systemic delivery and local autocrine production

evidence.snippet: The enzyme, aromatase, is aberrantly expressed in endometriotic stromal cells and catalyzes the conversion of C19 steroids to estrogens, which then stimulate cyclooxygenase-2 to increase the levels of PGE2. PGE2, in turn, is a potent inducer of aromatase activity in endometriotic stromal cells. Aromatase is not expressed in the eutopic endometrium.
evidence.explanation: Aromatase expression in endometriotic stromal cells creates a positive feedback loop with PGE2 for local estrogen production

evidence.snippet: In addition, we find that endometriotic tissue is deficient in 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, which is normally expressed in eutopic endometrial glandular cells and inactivates estradiol-17beta to estrone. This deficiency is another aberration that favors higher levels of estradiol-17beta in endometriotic tissues in comparison with the eutopic endometrium.
evidence.explanation: Deficiency of 17beta-HSD type 2 prevents estradiol inactivation, contributing to local estrogen dominance

steps/8.description: Endometriotic lesions produce their own estrogen via aromatase and are highly estrogen-responsive. Progesterone resistance impairs normal tissue regression.

Graded separately from the tissue arm because it is a different study type.

evidence.snippet: In vivo, we demonstrated that IL-33 significantly exacerbated endometriosis and induced hyperalgesia in mice. By interacting with the ST2 receptor in macrophages, IL-33 enhanced the release of tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α) and Interleukin 1β (IL-1β).
evidence.explanation: Murine endometriosis model linking a peritoneal danger signal to macrophage cytokine release and to hyperalgesia, which is the immune half of the inflammation-to-nociceptor edge feeding this node. The cascade has not been confirmed in human endometriosis tissue.

evidence.snippet: Ultimately, macrophage-derived TNF-α increased TRPV1 protein level in DRG neuronal cells through the TNFR1/p38 MAPK signaling pathway.
evidence.explanation: Cell-based arm identifying the receptor and kinase steps by which a macrophage cytokine raises TRPV1 in sensory neurons, converging on the same channel that human peritoneal tissue over-expresses.

steps/12.description: Lesion and peritoneal mediators, including inflammatory mediators and prolactin/prolactin-receptor signaling, can sensitize pelvic nociceptive sensory neurons. Human peritoneum and lesions over-express the nociceptive transducer and voltage-gated channels TRPV1, TRPA1, SCN11A and SCN9A, and estradiol raises TRPV1 in sensory neurons, so the sensitized state is both inflammatory and hormonally amplified. This provides a mechanism by which pain may be amplified without requiring proportional increases in lesion burden.

steps/13.description: Chronic inflammation leads to fibrous adhesions distorting pelvic anatomy. Adhesions contribute to pain and infertility.

evidence.snippet: Our results showed widespread alterations in pain thresholds in women with persistent pelvic pain that are indicative of central sensitization and a time-dependent correlation.
evidence.explanation: Human quantitative sensory testing supports central sensitization in persistent pelvic pain cohorts evaluated for suspected endometriosis.

evidence.snippet: Endometriosis is an inflammatory chronic condition associated with nociceptive, neuropathic, and nociplastic pain. Central sensitization (CS) is the primary nociplastic pain mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence supports modeling central sensitization as the main nociplastic pain mechanism in endometriosis-related chronic pelvic pain.

evidence.snippet: Patients with CSS have smaller changes in pain scores after endometriosis surgery (RR 0.79, confidence interval 0.73-0.86) and significantly higher persistent pain (RR 2.27, confidence interval 1.40-3.68).
evidence.explanation: Human clinical meta-analysis supports central sensitization as a treatment-response modifier associated with persistent post-surgical pain.

evidence.snippet: Significant decreased pain perception in both pain measurements (pressure pain threshold and numerical rating scale score) was found for the active tDCS group compared with the placebo group.
evidence.explanation: A randomized cortical neuromodulation trial supports central pain processing as a treatment-relevant component of endometriosis-associated chronic pelvic pain.

evidence.snippet: Relative to age-matched pain-free controls, women with endometriosis-associated CPP displayed increased levels of combined glutamine-glutamate (Glx) within the anterior insula and greater anterior insula connectivity to the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC).
evidence.explanation: Adds a brain-level correlate to a node otherwise built on sensory testing and questionnaires: excitatory neurotransmitter concentration and salience network connectivity differ in patients with pain. Two limits are load-bearing and are why this is not stronger evidence than it looks. The same study found no significant difference in endometriosis patients without pelvic pain, and its authors conclude the change may operate independently of the presence of endometriosis, so the signature tracks chronic pelvic pain rather than the disease. Group sizes are small (17 with pain, 13 without).

steps/14.description: Chronic endometriosis-associated pain can involve central nervous system amplification of pain signals and nociplastic pain mechanisms. This downstream state helps explain pain persistence and incomplete response to lesion-directed therapy in some patients.

evidence.snippet: Pain remains the cardinal symptom of endometriosis.
evidence.explanation: Supports pelvic pain as a central clinical phenotype of endometriosis; the existing frequency remains a broad clinical annotation rather than a quantitative claim from this snippet.

evidence.snippet: Endometriosis is usually classified into four stages: minimal, mild, moderate, and severe, though it is important to note that the presentation of symptoms does not necessarily correspond to the disease progression.
evidence.explanation: Supports the issue focus that symptoms, including pain, do not map cleanly to conventional disease-stage or progression measures.

steps/15.description: Chronic pelvic pain is a cardinal symptomatic burden of endometriosis and may be cyclical, non-cyclical, or persistent after lesion-directed therapy when sensitization mechanisms are established.

edges/0.description: Retrograde flow can deliver endometrial cells that already harbor cancer-associated mutations to ectopic sites, where they gain a selective advantage and expand clonally.

edges/1.description: Cancer-driver mutations confer a selective growth advantage that drives clonal expansion of the epithelial compartment at ectopic sites.

edges/2.description: Selective expansion of mutated endometrial epithelium at ectopic sites contributes to establishment of endometriosis lesions.

edges/3.description: The inflammatory peritoneal microenvironment provides prostaglandin, cytokine, and growth-factor signals that can couple lesion survival to neural and vascular remodeling.

edges/4.description: Inflammatory and hormonal mediators from the lesion/peritoneal compartment can lower nociceptor thresholds and amplify pelvic pain signaling.

edges/5.description: TGF-beta1 in the inflammatory peritoneal fluid drives peritoneal mesothelial cells toward the glycolytic (Warburg-like) phenotype.

edges/6.description: Progesterone resistance prevents progesterone-driven induction of 17beta-HSD-2, so estradiol is not inactivated and local estrogen levels stay high — reinforcing the estrogen-dependent growth of lesions.

edges/7.description: Angiogenic lesion programs can coexist with or promote nerve-fiber recruitment in endometriotic implants and adjacent peritoneal tissue.

edges/8.description: Lactate secreted by the glycolytic peritoneal microenvironment is implicated in supporting angiogenesis and lesion invasion, coupling the metabolic shift to the angiogenic program.

edges/9.description: Newly recruited lesion-associated nerve fibers and neurotrophic factors provide a peripheral substrate that can feed nociceptor sensitization.

edges/10.description: Persistent peripheral nociceptive input can contribute to central amplification and broader nociplastic pain processing.

edges/11.description: Sensitized pelvic nociceptors amplify the chronic pelvic pain phenotype.

edges/12.description: Central amplification can sustain or worsen pelvic pain even when lesion-directed treatment reduces peripheral disease activity.

genes/0.notes: GWAS-implicated susceptibility locus; no supporting evidence item curated yet.

genes/1.notes: GWAS-implicated susceptibility locus; no supporting evidence item curated yet.

genes/2.notes: GWAS-implicated susceptibility locus; no supporting evidence item curated yet.

genes/3.notes: GWAS-implicated susceptibility locus; no supporting evidence item curated yet.

evidence.snippet: One patient harbored two different KRAS mutations, c.35G→T and c.35G→C, and another carried identical KRAS c.35G→A mutations in three distinct lesions.
evidence.explanation: Recurrent activating KRAS codon-12 (c.35) mutations were validated in the epithelium of deep-infiltrating endometriotic lesions.

genes/4.notes: Recurrent activating KRAS mutations (e.g. c.35G>A/T/C) in the epithelial compartment of endometriotic lesions, with rising mutant-allele frequency relative to normal endometrium.

evidence.snippet: Five patients harbored known cancer driver mutations in ARID1A, PIK3CA, KRAS, or PPP2R1A, which were validated by Safe-Sequencing System or immunohistochemical analysis.
evidence.explanation: PIK3CA is among the validated somatic cancer-driver mutations found in deep-infiltrating endometriotic lesions.

evidence.snippet: Five patients harbored known cancer driver mutations in ARID1A, PIK3CA, KRAS, or PPP2R1A, which were validated by Safe-Sequencing System or immunohistochemical analysis.
evidence.explanation: ARID1A is among the validated somatic cancer-driver mutations found in deep-infiltrating endometriotic lesions.

evidence.snippet: Five patients harbored known cancer driver mutations in ARID1A, PIK3CA, KRAS, or PPP2R1A, which were validated by Safe-Sequencing System or immunohistochemical analysis.
evidence.explanation: PPP2R1A is among the validated somatic cancer-driver mutations found in deep-infiltrating endometriotic lesions.

evidence.snippet: Somatic mutations in the PTEN gene were identified in 4 of 20 ovarian endometrioid carcinomas (20.0%), 2 of 24 clear cell carcinomas (8.3%), and 7 of 34 solitary endometrial cysts (20.6%).
evidence.explanation: Somatic PTEN mutations are present in a fifth of ovarian endometriotic cysts, evidencing PTEN inactivation as an early somatic event in the endometriosis-to-ovarian-cancer sequence.

genes/8.notes: PTEN somatic point mutations and 10q23.3 loss of heterozygosity occur in ovarian endometriotic (endometrioma) cysts, consistent with the endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer (EAOC) continuum rather than the deep-infiltrating epithelial driver set.

treatments/0.description: First-line for pain management.

treatments/1.description: Suppress ovulation and reduce menstruation.

treatments/2.description: Create hypoestrogenic state (dienogest, medroxyprogesterone).

treatments/3.description: Induce medical menopause, add-back therapy needed.

treatments/4.description: Elagolix with dose-dependent estrogen suppression.

treatments/5.description: Reduce local estrogen production in lesions.

evidence.snippet: Oral DCA reduced peritoneal fluid lactate concentrations and endometriosis lesion size in a mouse model.
evidence.explanation: Oral dichloroacetate lowered peritoneal lactate and reduced lesion size in a mouse model, providing the in vivo rationale for clinical testing.

evidence.snippet: We plan a single-arm, open-label, single site exploratory clinical trial to inform the design of a future randomised controlled trial (RCT) to determine the efficacy of DCA for the treatment of endometriosis-associated pain.
evidence.explanation: The EPiC exploratory trial evaluates dichloroacetate in women with endometriosis-associated pain to inform a future efficacy RCT.

treatments/6.description: Investigational non-hormonal, non-contraceptive metabolic therapy. The pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK) inhibitor / PDH activator dichloroacetate reverses the aberrant glycolytic phenotype of peritoneal mesothelial cells, reduces lactate secretion, and shrank lesions in a mouse model; a single-arm open-label feasibility trial (EPiC) is evaluating it for endometriosis-associated pain ahead of a planned placebo-controlled trial.

evidence.snippet: Treatment of endometriosis HPMCs with the pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK) inhibitor/PDH activator dichloroacetate (DCA) normalizes HPMC metabolism, reduces lactate secretion, and abrogates endometrial stromal cell proliferation in a coculture model.
evidence.explanation: DCA reverses the Warburg-like metabolic phenotype and suppresses stromal proliferation in a coculture model, defining the targeted mechanism.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: DCA inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase and reactivates PDH, normalizing the glycolytic shift and reducing lactate secretion by peritoneal mesothelial cells.

evidence.snippet: A significant decrease in the percentage of active endometriotic lesions (P < 0.05) and cellular proliferation index (P < 0.001) was found with Cb2 treatment.
evidence.explanation: In a nude-mouse model of endometriosis, cabergoline reduced active lesions and proliferation, supporting anti-angiogenic therapeutic potential.

treatments/7.description: Investigational non-hormonal anti-angiogenic therapy. The dopamine D2 receptor agonist cabergoline promotes VEGF receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) endocytosis, preventing VEGF-VEGFR-2 binding and reducing neoangiogenesis. In experimentally induced endometriosis it decreased the proportion of active lesions and vascularization, and it is being evaluated as a non-hormonal, non-surgical option for endometriosis pain.

evidence.snippet: Cb2 treatment in experimental endometriosis has an anti-angiogenic effect acting through VEGFR-2 activation.
evidence.explanation: Cabergoline's anti-angiogenic action on endometriotic lesions operates through VEGFR-2, targeting the hypoxia/angiogenesis mechanism node.

treatments/7/targets/0.description: Dopamine-agonist-driven VEGFR-2 endocytosis and reduced VEGFR-2 phosphorylation blunt VEGF signaling and lesion neoangiogenesis.

treatments/8.description: Excision or ablation of lesions, adhesiolysis.

evidence.snippet: Increasing evidence points towards a close interaction between peripheral nerves, the peritoneal environment and the central nervous system in pain generation and processing.
evidence.explanation: Supports the integrated peripheral-peritoneal-central framing of the neuroimmune pain hypothesis.

evidence.snippet: The women with persistent pelvic pain had significantly lower pain thresholds compared with the reference women.
evidence.explanation: Human sensory-testing data support sensitization as part of the endometriosis-associated pelvic pain model.

evidence.snippet: Identified signals explained up to 5.01% of disease variance and regulated expression or methylation of genes in endometrium and blood, many of which were associated with pain perception/maintenance (SRP14/BMF, GDAP1, MLLT10, BSN and NGF).
evidence.explanation: Genetic support that is orthogonal to the tissue and imaging evidence for this model: risk loci from 60,674 cases act through genes involved in pain perception and maintenance, NGF among them. This implicates neurotrophin biology in disease susceptibility; it does not by itself demonstrate an NGF-to-pain causal chain in patients.

evidence.snippet: We observed significant genetic correlations between endometriosis and 11 pain conditions, including migraine, back and multisite chronic pain (MCP), as well as inflammatory conditions, including asthma and osteoarthritis.
evidence.explanation: Shared genetic architecture with unrelated chronic pain conditions supports treating endometriosis pain as partly a trait of central pain processing rather than solely a local lesion effect, which is the claim that distinguishes this hypothesis from a purely lesion-driven account.

evidence.snippet: Pain intensity did not differ significantly between rASRM stages I/II and III/IV (p > 0.05), though chronic pelvic pain was more frequent in advanced disease (p < 0.05).
evidence.explanation: Meta-analytic test of this hypothesis's signature prediction, replacing a narrative-review assertion of stage-symptom discordance with a pooled result across eight studies. The second half of the sentence is a genuine qualifier and is why the hypothesis stays EMERGING: pain intensity is stage-independent, but chronic pelvic pain frequency still rises with stage, so lesion burden is not wholly uninformative.

hypotheses/0.description: Endometriosis-associated pain is driven by lesion- and peritoneal microenvironment signals that promote neuroangiogenesis, peripheral nociceptor sensitization, and later central sensitization, so pain severity can persist or amplify independently of visible lesion burden.

evidence.snippet: Despite its prevalence, the underlying molecular mechanisms of this disease remain poorly understood.
evidence.explanation: Supports retaining lesion-independent pain mechanisms as an open curation gap rather than a fully settled causal chain.

evidence.snippet: However, a clear link between these findings and pain in patients with endometriosis has so far not been demonstrated.
evidence.explanation: Supports the unresolved gap between peripheral neuroangiogenic findings and patient-level pain severity.

evidence.snippet: Central sensitization (CSS), a condition where the central nervous system amplifies pain signals, may impact response to treatment of chronic pain conditions.
evidence.explanation: Supports the treatment-response component of the gap: central sensitization may modify response to lesion-directed therapy.

evidence.snippet: The study found no significant differences in EAPP reduction from baseline between groups and no significant dose-response model.
evidence.explanation: The negative P2X3 antagonist trial qualifies the neuroimmune pain model: not every plausible nociceptor-sensitization mediator has translated into clinical efficacy.

open_questions/0.rationale: The entry now models a neuroimmune pain circuit, but the relative causal weights of lesion-local innervation, soluble mediators, peripheral nociceptor threshold shifts, and central pain amplification remain unresolved. This gap determines whether patients should be stratified primarily by lesion phenotype, molecular/peritoneal mediator profile, quantitative sensory testing, or central-sensitization/nociplastic-pain measures when predicting persistent pain after lesion-directed treatment.

evidence.snippet: Our single-cell atlas revealed fundamentally distinct cellular ecosystems. EcP was enriched for CCL19 + perivascular cells (6.4-fold vs. control) and immune-active niches, whereas EcO exhibited pronounced smooth muscle differentiation and NNMT upregulation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the immune microenvironment differs sharply between peritoneal and ovarian lesions, which is the premise of the gap. It is an integrative reanalysis of previously published transcriptomes and reports no neural or nociceptive measurement, so it raises the subtype question without answering it.

evidence.snippet: There was a statistically significant difference in the prevalence of elevated FM Survey score between the endometriosis group and controls (41.7% vs. 0%, p = 0.045).
evidence.explanation: Cuts against a clean subtype restriction: nociplastic pain features are common in ovarian endometriosis, the subtype the transcriptomic contrast would predict to be least neuroimmune. A 12-patient pilot cannot settle this, which is exactly why the question stays open.

open_questions/1.rationale: Transcriptomic comparison separates the two commonest lesion types into an immune-active peritoneal niche and a fibromuscular ovarian one, which invites the conclusion that a chemokine and macrophage driven pain circuit should be a peritoneal and deep infiltrating phenomenon. That conclusion is not yet earned. The transcriptomic work carries no nerve fibre, neurotrophin, or nociceptive ion-channel readout at all, so it cannot locate the pain circuit; and the one study that measured nociplastic pain features specifically in ovarian endometriosis found them common there. Until neurotrophin and ion-channel expression is profiled across matched subtypes in the same patients, the entry models one circuit for the disease and records the subtype question here rather than restricting the hypothesis to a subset of lesions. The answer decides whether pain-directed therapy should be selected by lesion type.

evidence.snippet: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD) comprise a continuum of neurodevelopmental and physical disabilities resulting from the teratogenic effects of prenatal alcohol exposure.
evidence.explanation: Establishes prenatal alcohol exposure as the cause of the whole spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Retinaldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (RALDH2) is required to activate RA signaling at the onset of gastrulation.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the enzyme whose activity is competed for and the stage at which it matters.

evidence.snippet: One of the models proposed to explain the teratogenic effects of EtOH in FASD is the competition between EtOH and ROL for the ADH and RALDH activities that are necessary for RA biosynthesis in the embryo
evidence.explanation: Records that this is one competing model of ethanol teratogenicity, which is why this node is curated as a route rather than as the mechanism.

steps/1.description: Retinoic acid is made from retinol in two oxidation steps, the second catalysed by retinaldehyde dehydrogenases, of which RALDH2 (ALDH1A2) is the one that switches retinoic acid signaling on at the start of gastrulation. Ethanol is a substrate for the same dehydrogenase activities, so an ethanol-exposed embryo diverts enzyme capacity away from retinoic acid synthesis. The competition model is one of several proposed accounts of ethanol teratogenicity, and is the one this entry curates.

evidence.snippet: In light of the multiple regulatory roles of RA, continued embryogenesis in the presence of abnormally low RA levels provides an etiological explanation for the malformations observed in individuals with FASD.
evidence.explanation: States the node's central claim in the authors' own terms, including its status as an explanation offered.

steps/2.description: With retinoic acid below its normal level from gastrulation onward, development does not stop — it continues, misdirected, in a signaling environment that patterns the head, eye, heart and nervous system. That continuation at abnormally low retinoic acid is what the model offers as the etiological explanation for a malformation pattern spread across several organ systems rather than confined to one.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the malformation pattern this node describes.

steps/3.description: The severe end of the spectrum, fetal alcohol syndrome, combines craniofacial malformation, microcephaly, growth restriction, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioural impairment. Milder positions on the continuum may carry the neurodevelopmental impairment without the recognizable physical features, which is a large part of why the diagnosis is missed.

evidence.snippet: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD) comprise a continuum of neurodevelopmental and physical disabilities resulting from the teratogenic effects of prenatal alcohol exposure.
evidence.explanation: States that neurodevelopmental disability is constitutive of the spectrum.

steps/4.description: The feature that defines the spectrum and is present across it, including in individuals without recognizable physical features.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists microcephaly among the cardinal features.

steps/5.description: Reduced head circumference, a cardinal feature of fetal alcohol syndrome.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists short stature among the cardinal features.

steps/6.description: Growth restriction, one of the growth criteria used in FASD diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists microphthalmia among the cardinal features.

steps/7.description: Reduced eye size, an ocular malformation consistent with a retinoic acid-dependent developmental mechanism.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists heart defects among the cardinal features.

steps/8.description: Congenital heart defects occur within the alcohol-related birth defect category.

evidence.snippet: In Xenopus embryos, ethanol reduces the levels of retinoic acid (RA) signaling during gastrulation.
evidence.explanation: The measured consequence that this edge asserts.

edges/0.description: Diverting retinaldehyde dehydrogenase capacity lowers embryonic retinoic acid at exactly the stage when the pathway is first switched on.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists the malformation pattern at the severe end of the spectrum; the attribution of that pattern to reduced retinoic acid is the paper's proposal, not a demonstrated result in humans.

edges/1.description: Retinoic acid patterns many structures, so a global reduction produces a distributed rather than an organ-specific malformation pattern.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists microcephaly among the features.

edges/2.description: Reduced brain growth is among the cardinal features at the severe end of the spectrum.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists short stature among the features.

edges/3.description: Growth restriction is part of the recognized pattern.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists microphthalmia among the features.

edges/4.description: Ocular involvement is expected under a retinoic-acid mechanism, since eye development is retinoic acid dependent.

evidence.snippet: The strongest manifestation of FASD, also known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), can include: craniofacial malformations, microcephaly, short stature, microphthalmia, heart defects and behavioral and psychological problems
evidence.explanation: Lists heart defects among the features.

edges/5.description: Congenital heart defects are part of the recognized pattern.

evidence.snippet: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD) comprise a continuum of neurodevelopmental and physical disabilities resulting from the teratogenic effects of prenatal alcohol exposure.
evidence.explanation: Establishes neurodevelopmental disability as spanning the continuum rather than being confined to the severe end.

edges/6.description: Neurodevelopmental disability is the feature present across the whole continuum, including where physical features are absent.

evidence.snippet: The biochemical evidence that we present shows that, at the onset of RA signaling during early gastrulation, the ethanol effect centers on the competition for the available retinaldehyde dehydrogenase activity.
evidence.explanation: States the biochemical step by which the exposure acts on this mechanism.

edges/7.description: Ethanol reaching the embryo competes with retinol and retinaldehyde for the same dehydrogenase activities, which is the initiating step of the mechanism curated here.

evidence.snippet: While most studies have found a protective effect for genotypes containing ADH1B*2 or ADH1B*3, results have been conflicting, and further investigation into the association between the ADH1B genotype and FAS is needed.
evidence.explanation: The pooled review reports a protective trend and states plainly that the results conflict, which is the level of support this entry records.

evidence.snippet: Studies of genetic associations with FAS have focused on the alcohol dehydrogenase 1B (ADH1B) gene, comparing mothers and children with the alleles ADH1B*2 or ADH1B*3, associated with faster ethanol metabolism, with those homozygous for ADH1B*1.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the mechanism by which this gene could modify risk — rate of ethanol elimination — which is the same competition-for-enzyme axis the pathophysiology of this entry runs on.

evidence.snippet: There were no statistically significant differences between the respective groups of genotypes of the studied polymorphisms.
evidence.explanation: A negative result in 303 children and 251 mothers, curated as refuting so the conflict is visible in the record rather than averaged away.

genes/0.notes: ADH1B*2 and ADH1B*3 metabolize ethanol faster, and the hypothesis is that either maternal or fetal fast-metabolizer genotypes shorten fetal exposure. The evidence does not settle it: a HuGE review found most studies reporting a protective effect but with conflicting results, and a later 303-child / 251-mother study found no significant genotype differences at all. Recorded as a candidate modifier with both results attached rather than as an established risk gene.

evidence.snippet: we considered three polymorphisms of genes implicated in the synthesis of enzymes involved in ethanol metabolism, i.e., ADH1b (rs1229984), ADH1b/c (rs1789891), and CYP2E1 (rs3813867)
evidence.explanation: Establishes that CYP2E1 rs3813867 was among the variants tested for a FASD association.

evidence.snippet: There were no statistically significant differences between the respective groups of genotypes of the studied polymorphisms.
evidence.explanation: The negative result covering CYP2E1 as well as ADH1B, recorded so the null finding is visible.

genes/1.notes: CYP2E1 provides the microsomal route of ethanol oxidation, which is induced by chronic intake and generates reactive oxygen species, so it is a plausible modifier on the same elimination-rate axis as ADH1B. The one study curated here tested rs3813867 with the ADH1B polymorphisms and found nothing significant.

evidence.snippet: abstaining from alcohol consumption during pregnancy is the safest and most effective strategy to prevent FASD
evidence.explanation: The prevention recommendation stated by a current diagnostic review.

treatments/0.description: The only intervention that addresses the cause. Because the mechanism curated here operates at gastrulation, prevention has to precede the point at which many pregnancies are recognized, which is why the recommendation is framed as abstinence rather than as reduction after a positive test.

evidence.snippet: One of the models proposed to explain the teratogenic effects of EtOH in FASD is the competition between EtOH and ROL for the ADH and RALDH activities that are necessary for RA biosynthesis in the embryo
evidence.explanation: Records that the curated route is one model among several.

open_questions/0.rationale: This entry was created to host a Xenopus model that makes a strong epistatic case for the retinoic acid route, and the pathograph reflects that model's scope rather than the state of the field. Presenting one route without the others risks reading as a claim that the question is settled, which it is not. The competing mechanisms are named in the same paper's introduction and each has its own literature.

evidence.snippet: FASD remains frequently underrecognized or misdiagnosed
evidence.explanation: Underdiagnosis is what makes precise dysmorphology criteria worth curating rather than a bookkeeping detail.

open_questions/1.rationale: The 2016 updated diagnostic guidelines are now cited, and the `diagnosis` section records the dysmorphology scoring system and lip/philtrum guide that grade the facial component. What is still missing is the triad itself as three bound HP phenotypes: the guideline abstract describes revising the criteria without stating them, and this entry's evidence policy requires an exact quote that substantively supports the claim, so the features are omitted rather than sourced to a paraphrase. A full-text guideline record or a review that states the triad explicitly would close this.

evidence.snippet: 14q22q23 microdeletion syndrome, also called Frias syndrome, is an extremely rare partial deletion of the long arm of chromosome 14 characterized by the anomalies of the pituitary gland, eyes, and hand/foot.
evidence.explanation: This defines Frias syndrome as a partial 14q deletion with the core organ systems represented in this pathophysiology graph.

evidence.snippet: This case report presents the case of a young child with a deletion in 14q22.2q23.1 region containing both BMP4 and OTX2 genes as well as sineoculis homeobox homolog 1 (SIX1) and sineoculis homeobox homolog 6 (SIX6) genes.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports inclusion of BMP4, OTX2, SIX1, and SIX6 as recurrent genes within the deleted interval.

steps/0.description: The initiating lesion is a heterozygous interstitial deletion of the 14q22-q23 region. Variable deletion breakpoints alter gene content, which explains why ocular, endocrine, craniofacial, limb, and neurodevelopmental manifestations vary across individuals.

evidence.snippet: The 6.5 Mb deletion contains 27 genes, including three genes of the SIX family: SIX1, SIX4, and SIX6.
evidence.explanation: This supports loss of SIX-family genes in a 14q22.3-q23.2 deletion case.

evidence.snippet: In mammals, Six1 has been shown to be involved in ocular differentiation, whereas Six4 and Six6 are primarily expressed in the hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and facial bones.
evidence.explanation: This mouse-expression and comparative-development evidence supports the ocular, pituitary, hypothalamic, and craniofacial mechanism assigned to SIX-region dosage loss.

evidence.snippet: In this report, we describe a case of large microdeletion encompassing OTX2 but not BMP4 presenting with a syndromic anophthalmia with corpus callosum hypoplasia, pituitary gland hypoplasia and vermian hypoplasia.
evidence.explanation: This supports OTX2-region deletion as sufficient for major ocular, pituitary, corpus-callosum, and cerebellar-vermis phenotypes.

steps/1.description: Dosage loss of OTX2 and neighboring SIX-family genes disrupts ocular, pituitary, hypothalamic, facial-bone, and brain developmental programs.

evidence.snippet: This gene family plays an important role during early embryogenesis, and the complex synergistic functions and redundancies of the BMPs led us to conclude that haploinsufficiency of BMP4 is likely to be responsible for the clinical expression of Frías syndrome.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports BMP4 haploinsufficiency as a causal mechanism for the syndrome.

evidence.snippet: BMP4 has a number of roles in embryonic development including neurogenesis, lens induction, development of cartilage and bone, urogenital development, limb and digit patterning, hair follicle regeneration, as well as tooth formation.
evidence.explanation: This supports the developmental-process annotations and links BMP4 dosage loss to eye, limb, skeletal, and other congenital findings.

steps/2.description: BMP4 dosage loss disrupts BMP/TGF-beta developmental signaling. This affects embryonic morphogenesis, eye development, skeletal development, and limb/digit patterning, contributing to ocular, craniofacial, and hand/foot findings.

evidence.snippet: Interstitial microdeletion 14q22q23 is a rare chromosomal syndrome associated with variable defects: microphthalmia/anophthalmia, pituitary anomalies, polydactyly/syndactyly of hands and feet, micrognathia/retrognathia.
evidence.explanation: This directly lists microphthalmia/anophthalmia among the variable defects of 14q22q23 microdeletion syndrome.

steps/3.description: Microphthalmia is a defining congenital ocular manifestation in the 14q22q23 deletion spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Mutations of BMP4 and OTX2 often lead to eye defects, including anophthalmia-microphthalmia.
evidence.explanation: This supports severe ocular malformations when BMP4 and OTX2 are deleted or mutated.

steps/4.description: Anophthalmia represents the severe end of the congenital ocular malformation spectrum in Frias syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Interstitial microdeletion 14q22q23 is a rare chromosomal syndrome associated with variable defects: microphthalmia/anophthalmia, pituitary anomalies, polydactyly/syndactyly of hands and feet, micrognathia/retrognathia.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports micrognathia/retrognathia in the phenotype spectrum.

steps/5.description: Micrognathia or retrognathia can be detected prenatally and is part of the orofacial phenotype.

evidence.snippet: In this report, we describe a case of large microdeletion encompassing OTX2 but not BMP4 presenting with a syndromic anophthalmia with corpus callosum hypoplasia, pituitary gland hypoplasia and vermian hypoplasia.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports pituitary gland hypoplasia in an OTX2-region deletion; HP:0010627 is used as the closest available HPO term after a targeted OAK lookup did not identify a general pituitary-gland hypoplasia class.

steps/6.description: Pituitary hypoplasia is a core endocrine manifestation of the deletion syndrome. The local HPO cache does not expose a separate general "pituitary gland hypoplasia" term, so this entry uses anterior pituitary hypoplasia as the closest phenotype-level HPO mapping.

evidence.snippet: Mutations occurring in the orthodenticle homeobox 2 gene (OTX2) are responsible for a rare genetic syndrome, characterized mainly by microphthalmia/anophthalmia associated with extra-ocular defects such as brain malformations, pituitary abnormalities, short stature and intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports short stature among OTX2-region deletion features.

steps/7.description: Short stature is part of the extra-ocular phenotype associated with OTX2 disruption.

evidence.snippet: Interstitial microdeletion 14q22q23 is a rare chromosomal syndrome associated with variable defects: microphthalmia/anophthalmia, pituitary anomalies, polydactyly/syndactyly of hands and feet, micrognathia/retrognathia.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports polydactyly in the hand/foot phenotype.

steps/8.description: Supernumerary digits may occur as part of the hand/foot anomaly spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Interstitial microdeletion 14q22q23 is a rare chromosomal syndrome associated with variable defects: microphthalmia/anophthalmia, pituitary anomalies, polydactyly/syndactyly of hands and feet, micrognathia/retrognathia.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports syndactyly in the hand/foot phenotype.

steps/9.description: Webbing or fusion of digits can accompany polydactyly in the hand/foot anomaly spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Intellectual disability and facial dysmorphism are other common manifestations.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports intellectual disability as a common feature.

evidence.snippet: In this report, we describe a case of large microdeletion encompassing OTX2 but not BMP4 presenting with a syndromic anophthalmia with corpus callosum hypoplasia, pituitary gland hypoplasia and vermian hypoplasia.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports corpus callosum hypoplasia.

steps/11.description: Corpus callosum hypoplasia can occur in OTX2-region 14q22q23 deletions.

evidence.snippet: In this report, we describe a case of large microdeletion encompassing OTX2 but not BMP4 presenting with a syndromic anophthalmia with corpus callosum hypoplasia, pituitary gland hypoplasia and vermian hypoplasia.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports cerebellar vermis hypoplasia.

steps/12.description: Vermian hypoplasia broadens the brain-malformation spectrum of OTX2-region deletions.

evidence.snippet: A review of twelve previously reported patients with 14q22 microdeletion revealed decreased white matter volume in half of the patients.
evidence.explanation: This supports cerebral white matter morphology abnormality in the 14q22 microdeletion spectrum.

edges/13.description: Severe OTX2-region ocular developmental disruption can prevent globe formation.

evidence.snippet: We report a detection of the microdeletion 14q22.1q23.1 spanning 7,7 Mb and involving the genes BMP4 and OTX2 in the foetus by multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) and verified by microarray subsequently.
evidence.explanation: This supports a causal 14q22q23 copy-number deletion involving BMP4 and OTX2 and detected by CNV methods.

evidence.snippet: The 6.5 Mb deletion contains 27 genes, including three genes of the SIX family: SIX1, SIX4, and SIX6.
evidence.explanation: This supports SIX1/SIX4/SIX6 inclusion in some pathogenic 14q22-q23 deletions.

evidence.snippet: The patients should be provided with genetic counselling.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports genetic counseling in the context of suspected or confirmed prenatal 14q22q23 microdeletion.

treatments/0.description: Genetic counseling is important because both de novo and familial deletions have been reported, and prenatal detection is possible when fetal anomalies raise suspicion.

evidence.snippet: 14q22q23 microdeletion syndrome, also called Frias syndrome, is an extremely rare partial deletion of the long arm of chromosome 14 characterized by the anomalies of the pituitary gland, eyes, and hand/foot.
evidence.explanation: This supports the multisystem congenital presentation that requires phenotype-directed supportive care; the abstract does not describe a syndrome-specific curative treatment.

evidence.snippet: Here, we present a 12-year-old girl with dysmorphic face, choanal atresia, gastroesophageal reflux, and moderate developmental delay, in whom an interstitial deletion 14q22.3-q23.2 was detected using a 180k array comparative genome hybridization.
evidence.explanation: This case report documents craniofacial, airway, gastrointestinal, and neurodevelopmental manifestations that support symptom-directed supportive care.

treatments/1.description: Supportive care is phenotype-directed across the multisystem presentation, including ophthalmologic, endocrine, neurodevelopmental, craniofacial, hand/foot, gastrointestinal, and airway manifestations when present.

evidence.snippet: Biallelic variants in HFM1 cause human male infertility owing to non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) with impaired crossover formation and meiotic metaphase I (MMI) arrest.
evidence.explanation: Establishes impaired crossover formation as the direct consequence of biallelic HFM1 variants in human infertility.

evidence.snippet: These Hfm1 variants led to various reductions of HFM1 foci on chromosome axes and resulted in varying degrees of synapsis and crossover formation defects in the mutant male mice.
evidence.explanation: Mouse models of patient HFM1 variants recapitulate synapsis and crossover defects, linking reduced HFM1 foci to defective meiotic recombination.

steps/1.description: Biallelic HFM1 loss disables the helicase activity required to process recombination intermediates into designated crossovers during meiotic prophase I. HFM1 stabilizes the MutSγ complex (MSH4-MSH5) on Holliday junctions and promotes class I crossover formation. Its loss leads to varying reductions in HFM1 foci on chromosome axes and defects in synapsis and crossover formation, blocking meiotic progression.

evidence.snippet: Hfm1 mutant female mice displayed infertility or subfertility with oogenesis variously affected.
evidence.explanation: Mouse models demonstrate germ-cell failure in both sexes on HFM1 loss, consistent with the pachytene/metaphase arrest and germ-cell depletion pathway.

steps/2.description: Germ cells that cannot complete meiotic crossover formation arrest at meiotic metaphase I and are eliminated by apoptosis rather than maturing into functional gametes, depleting the germ-cell pool in both sexes.

evidence.snippet: We recruited 24 patients with POI and identified variants in POI-related genes in 14 patients, including bi-allelic mutations in DNAH6, HFM1, EIF2B2, BNC, and LRPPRC.
evidence.explanation: WES cohort confirms biallelic HFM1 variants as a cause of primary ovarian insufficiency in 46,XX individuals.

evidence.snippet: Apart from NOA and POI, biallelic variants in HFM1 were also associated with recurrent implantation failure (RIF).
evidence.explanation: Documents the full female phenotypic spectrum of HFM1 deficiency from POI to poor ovarian response and recurrent implantation failure.

steps/3.description: Loss of oocytes during meiotic crossover failure depletes the ovarian reserve. 46,XX individuals present with primary ovarian insufficiency, poor ovarian response in IVF cycles, and/or recurrent implantation failure. The severity varies: some individuals have amenorrhea and ovarian dysgenesis while others have oligomenorrhea or subfertility.

evidence.snippet: Testicular histological analysis revealed that spermatogenesis is arrested at MMI in patients carrying the variants.
evidence.explanation: Direct histological evidence of spermatogenic arrest at metaphase I in men with biallelic HFM1 variants, establishing the male phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Our results showed that a deleterious splicing variant in HFM1 was related to NOA in these two patients.
evidence.explanation: Additional independent NOA family with a splicing variant in HFM1 confirms the male infertility phenotype.

steps/4.description: In 46,XY individuals, HFM1-dependent meiotic failure produces spermatogenic arrest at meiotic metaphase I. Testicular histology shows complete arrest of spermatogenesis; no retrievable spermatozoa are found on microTESE, and patients present with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) or, in some cases with hypomorphic variants, severe oligozoospermia amenable to ICSI.

evidence.snippet: We recruited 24 patients with POI and identified variants in POI-related genes in 14 patients, including bi-allelic mutations in DNAH6, HFM1, EIF2B2, BNC, and LRPPRC.
evidence.explanation: WES cohort identifies biallelic HFM1 as a cause of POI in 46,XX individuals.

steps/5.description: Reported 46,XX individuals present with primary ovarian insufficiency, often with poor ovarian response, recurrent implantation failure, or complete amenorrhea.

evidence.snippet: Histopathology of the testis showed that spermatogenesis was completely blocked at metaphase in these two patients carrying the HFM1 homozygous variants.
evidence.explanation: Testicular histopathology shows metaphase I arrest in patients with biallelic HFM1 variants, confirming the recombination failure to meiotic arrest to azoospermia pathway.

edges/1.description: Unresolved meiotic recombination intermediates block germ-cell progression through prophase I and trigger germ-cell apoptosis.

edges/2.description: In 46,XX individuals, germ-cell depletion exhausts the ovarian follicle pool and produces primary ovarian insufficiency.

edges/3.description: In 46,XY individuals, the same germ-cell depletion produces spermatogenic failure presenting as non-obstructive azoospermia.

edges/4.description: The female branch presents clinically as primary or premature ovarian insufficiency, with variable severity from poor ovarian response to complete ovarian failure.

treatments/0.description: Genetic counseling for couples with biallelic HFM1 variants. Assisted reproductive technology outcomes depend on residual HFM1 function: complete loss-of-function in 46,XY individuals typically makes microTESE unsuccessful (sperm retrieval rate is low); hypomorphic variants may allow ICSI with the few available spermatozoa. For 46,XX individuals, oocyte cryopreservation before complete ovarian failure may preserve fertility if the diagnosis is made early.

treatments/1.description: Estrogen-progestogen hormone replacement therapy is standard of care for 46,XX individuals with HFM1-related primary ovarian insufficiency, addressing bone density, cardiovascular risk, and menopausal symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Three of these mutations were nonsense (p.R63X, p.R112X, p.Y275X) and five were missense mutations (p.T297A, p.R417H, p.R417C, p.F470I, p.R486C), the last four clustering in exon 6 at the C-terminal end of the protein. Residue R417 appeared as a mutational hot-spot.
evidence.explanation: The allelic spectrum and the hot-spot residue.

steps/1.description: Biallelic CYP7B1 variants reduce or abolish oxysterol 7alpha-hydroxylase, a cytochrome P450 expressed in brain and liver. Reported alleles include nonsense changes (p.R63X, p.R112X, p.Y275X) and missense changes clustering at the C-terminal end of the protein in exon 6, with residue R417 recurring often enough to be described as a mutational hot spot.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrate here that four patients with the SPG5 disease have 6- to 9-fold increased plasma levels of 27-hydroxycholesterol. A much higher increase, 30- to 50-fold, was found in cerebrospinal fluid.
evidence.explanation: The compartment-specific magnitudes, measured in patients. The much larger CSF increase is the reason a central mechanism is plausible at all.

evidence.snippet: The pattern of bile acids in serum was normal, suggesting a normal bile acid synthesis.
evidence.explanation: Excludes a bile acid deficiency as the lesion, which is what distinguishes this disease from the neonatal cholestatic CYP7B1 phenotype.

steps/2.description: 27-hydroxycholesterol and 25-hydroxycholesterol accumulate. The magnitudes differ by compartment and by species of oxysterol in a way that matters: plasma 27-hydroxycholesterol rises 6- to 9-fold, cerebrospinal fluid 27-hydroxycholesterol 30- to 50-fold, and plasma 25-hydroxycholesterol about 100-fold, while 25-hydroxycholesterol is not measurable in cerebrospinal fluid at all. Bile acid synthesis itself is normal, so this is a substrate-stranding lesion and not a bile acid deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Oxysterols were found to impair metabolic activity and viability of human cortical neurons at concentrations found in SPG5 patients, indicating that elevated levels of oxysterols might be key pathogenic factors in SPG5.
evidence.explanation: The neurotoxicity result in human cells.

steps/3.description: Oxysterols at patient concentrations impair metabolic activity and viability of human cortical neurons. The experiment was done in human neurons and dosed to the levels measured in patients, which is the strongest link in this chain — but note it establishes that these concentrations are toxic to cortical neurons in culture, not that the same process selects the long corticospinal axons in vivo.

evidence.snippet: Spastic paraplegia type 5 (SPG5) is a rare subtype of hereditary spastic paraplegia, a highly heterogeneous group of neurodegenerative disorders defined by progressive neurodegeneration of the corticospinal tract motor neurons.
evidence.explanation: The defining lesion of the disease class, of which SPG5 is stated to be a member.

steps/4.description: Progressive degeneration of the corticospinal tract motor neurons is the defining lesion of hereditary spastic paraplegia as a class, and SPG5 is one instance of it. White matter hyperintensities on brain MRI accompany it in a substantial minority, including in families whose clinical phenotype is otherwise pure.

evidence.snippet: After a mean disease duration of 28.3 +/- 13.4 years (10-58), spasticity and functional handicap were moderate to severe in all cases.
evidence.explanation: Spasticity in every patient of this series, with the duration over which it accrued.

steps/5.description:
Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness, the defining clinical feature. Spasticity and functional handicap were moderate to severe in all cases after a mean disease duration of 28 years.
VERY_FREQUENT is supported by "in all cases" in the quoted series rather than being estimated from the disease definition.

evidence.snippet: Hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) is a neurodegenerative condition defined clinically by lower limb spasticity and weakness.
evidence.explanation: The clinical definition of the disease class this entry belongs to. It names the upper motor neuron syndrome of which hyperreflexia is part, so it supports the claim through an inference step rather than stating it.

steps/6.description: Brisk lower limb reflexes are part of the upper motor neuron syndrome that defines the disease class. No located source gives a frequency for reflex findings specifically in genetically confirmed SPG5, so the slot is left empty.

evidence.snippet: Gait ataxia was a common feature.
evidence.explanation: The paper's own frequency word in a 34-patient cohort.

steps/7.description:
A common feature, and one that complicates the historical classification of SPG5 as a pure spastic paraplegia — a pure HSP should not have prominent cerebellar signs. An earlier study separately found a coding polymorphism in CYP7B1 significantly associated with cerebellar signs complicating an HSP phenotype.
FREQUENT is the band that the source's word "common" maps to; no percentage is given anywhere in the located literature.

evidence.snippet: In addition, white matter hyperintensities were observed on brain magnetic resonance imaging in three patients issued from two of the seven pure families.
evidence.explanation: Three patients from two families, with the important detail that those families were clinically classified as pure.

steps/8.description: Seen on brain MRI, including in patients from families whose clinical phenotype is pure. Their presence is part of the argument that SPG5 is not as pure as its classification suggests.

evidence.snippet: Hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) is a neurodegenerative condition defined clinically by lower limb spasticity and weakness.
evidence.explanation: Supports the upper motor neuron syndrome that produces the bladder disturbance, through an inference step rather than by naming it.

steps/9.description: Bladder urgency is the usual genitourinary consequence of an upper motor neuron lesion in the spastic paraplegias. No located source quantifies it in genetically confirmed SPG5, so no frequency is recorded.

evidence.snippet: One of the expected metabolic consequences of such mutations is accumulation of oxysterol substrates due to decreased enzyme activity.
evidence.explanation: States the predicted consequence of the enzyme deficiency, which the same paper then confirms by measurement.

edges/1.description: The enzyme's substrates have no alternative route out, so they accumulate. The founding metabolic study framed this as the expected consequence and then measured it.

evidence.snippet: Oxysterols were found to impair metabolic activity and viability of human cortical neurons at concentrations found in SPG5 patients, indicating that elevated levels of oxysterols might be key pathogenic factors in SPG5.
evidence.explanation: The dose-matching is what makes this edge causal rather than a demonstration that a sterol can be toxic at some concentration.

edges/2.description: The accumulated oxysterols are themselves toxic to the relevant human neurons at the concentrations found in patients, which is the step that converts a biochemical abnormality into a mechanism.

edges/3.description: Why a diffuse metabolic insult produces a length-dependent degeneration of the corticospinal tract, rather than a generalised cortical disease, is not established in any located source.

edges/6.description: Gait ataxia is common in SPG5 and is not straightforwardly explained by corticospinal degeneration alone, which is part of why the "pure" classification of this disease has been questioned.

edges/7.description: Loss of descending corticospinal control of the detrusor produces urgency, the usual bladder consequence of an upper motor neuron lesion.

evidence.snippet: Very recently, five mutations in the CYP7B1 gene, encoding a cytochrome P450 oxysterol 7-alpha hydroxylase and expressed in brain and liver, have been found in SPG5 families.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the gene product and its expression pattern. The sentence is this paper's introduction summarising the prior gene-identification report.

evidence.snippet: The SPG5A subtype of Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia (HSP) is a rare autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by mutations in the CYP7B1 gene, which encodes a steroid cytochrome P450 7α-hydroxylase.
evidence.explanation: The gene-disease relationship stated for the SPG5A subtype by name.

evidence.snippet: Four novel mutations were identified; one frameshift (c.509 delT p.L170fs), one premature stop codon (c.334 C>T p.R112X), one amino acid changing (c.440 G>A p.G147D) and one duplication (c.945_947 dupGGC p.A316AA).
evidence.explanation: The four variant classes in one sentence, which is what makes the allelic spectrum recordable without assembling it from separate reports.

genes/0.notes:
Cytochrome P450 family 7 subfamily B member 1, encoding oxysterol 7alpha-hydroxylase and expressed in brain and liver. Biallelic variants cause SPG5.
The same gene separately causes congenital bile acid synthesis defect type 3, a neonatal cholestatic liver disease, which the dismech entry Inborn_Disorder_of_Bile_Acid_Synthesis already carries as a has_subtypes entry. The two are not a severity spectrum of one disease: in SPG5 the serum bile acid pattern is normal and the lesion is substrate accumulation, whereas the neonatal disease is a failure of bile acid production.

evidence.snippet: In cerebrospinal fluid 27-hydroxycholesterol was reduced by 8.4% but this did not significantly differ from placebo.
evidence.explanation: The negative half of the same trial, quoted as a separate evidence item because it bears on whether the drug reaches the compartment that matters. This is the limitation that keeps the treatment from being an established therapy.

treatments/0.description: Atorvastatin 40 mg/day for nine weeks lowered serum 27-hydroxycholesterol by 31.5% in a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in 14 SPG5 patients, against a primary endpoint of serum 27-hydroxycholesterol. Read the result carefully: the trial met a biomarker endpoint, not a clinical one; cerebrospinal fluid 27-hydroxycholesterol fell only 8.4% and did not separate from placebo; and no clinical effect was seen or expected over nine weeks. It is described by its authors as the first causal treatment strategy in hereditary spastic paraplegia, which is a claim about the strategy rather than about demonstrated clinical benefit.

evidence.snippet: Atorvastatin, but not placebo, reduced serum 27-hydroxycholesterol from 853 ng/ml
evidence.explanation: The randomised result on the primary endpoint, with its comparator. The quote stops before the interquartile range because the reference validator strips bracketed spans before matching; the full reported change is 853 to 641 ng/ml, a 31.5% reduction at P = 0.001, and is given in the treatment description.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Reducing cholesterol synthesis lowers the pool from which the stranded oxysterols are made, which is how a statin acts on a disease that is not a hypercholesterolaemia.

open_questions/0.rationale: The toxicity experiment that anchors this entry was done in human cortical neurons in culture and shows impaired viability at patient concentrations. It does not explain selectivity. Every hereditary spastic paraplegia has to answer this question and SPG5 has no better answer than the rest, so the edge from neurotoxicity to tract degeneration is typed with unknown intermediates.

open_questions/1.rationale: This is the hole in an otherwise unusually complete causal chain. Atorvastatin lowered serum 27-hydroxycholesterol by 31.5% with p = 0.001, but the cerebrospinal fluid reduction was 8.4% and did not separate from placebo — and cerebrospinal fluid is where the 30- to 50-fold accumulation sits. A biomarker trial that moves the peripheral marker without demonstrating central target engagement does not establish that the strategy can work, whatever the mechanism predicts.

open_questions/2.rationale: The knockout mouse accumulates 27-hydroxycholesterol and stays neurologically well, which taken alone argues against the oxysterol hypothesis. The dose figure rescues it — the mouse reaches about 20% of patient plasma levels — but "the model never reached the toxic concentration" and "the mouse tolerates concentrations that harm human neurons" are different claims with different consequences for using the model to test a therapy. No located source distinguishes them. This is a model-fidelity question rather than a plain absence of evidence, which is why it is typed HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH.

evidence.snippet: the VCP (p97 or CDC48) gene which plays a key role in the ubiquitin-proteasome dependent degradation of cytosolic proteins and in the retro translocation of misfolded proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm.
evidence.explanation: This review links disease-causing VCP variants to protein quality-control functions.

steps/3.description: Pathogenic VCP variants perturb the AAA+ ATPase functions that normally coordinate ubiquitin-dependent protein turnover and retrotranslocation of misfolded endoplasmic-reticulum proteins, creating the proximal proteostasis defect in classic IBMPFD.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that VCP is essential for autophagosome maturation.
evidence.explanation: Cell-based experiments directly establish VCP as required for autophagosome maturation.

evidence.snippet: expression of disease-associated VCP mutants (R155H and A232E) also causes this autophagy defect.
evidence.explanation: Disease-associated VCP alleles reproduce the autophagy defect in experimental cells.

evidence.snippet: This is likely due to a defect in p97/VCP-mediated autophagosome maturation.
evidence.explanation: Review-level evidence links IBMPFD VCP mutations to defective autophagosome maturation.

steps/4.description: VCP is required for autophagosome maturation under basal and proteasome stress conditions. Disease-associated VCP variants produce enlarged, ubiquitin-positive autophagic vesicles and patient-derived myoblast vacuoles, linking the upstream proteostasis defect to IBMPFD tissue pathology.

evidence.snippet: the autophagosomes that accumulate due to impaired VCP function contain ubiquitin-positive contents.
evidence.explanation: Experimental data show that impaired VCP function leaves ubiquitin-positive cargo in autophagosomes.

evidence.snippet: Inclusions seen in the muscle, brain and heart in VCP disease contain ubiquitin, beta amyloid and TDP-43
evidence.explanation: Human pathology evidence supports multisystem ubiquitin-positive inclusion pathology.

steps/5.description: Impaired clearance of ubiquitinated autophagic cargo produces persistent ubiquitin-positive inclusions and vacuoles in affected muscle and brain, aligning the molecular defect with the hallmark proteinopathy.

evidence.snippet: Wild-type hnRNPA2 (the most abundant isoform of hnRNPA2B1) and hnRNPA1 show an intrinsic tendency to assemble into self-seeding fibrils, which is exacerbated by the disease mutations.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that both proteins self-assemble into fibrils and that the disease variants increase that assembly, which is the state this node asserts.

evidence.snippet: Indeed, the pathogenic mutations strengthen a 'steric zipper' motif in the PrLD, which accelerates the formation of self-seeding fibrils that cross-seed polymerization of wild-type hnRNP.
evidence.explanation: Names the steric zipper motif and the cross-seeding of wild-type protein stated in this node's description, and is the sentence supporting the protein polymerization binding. Graded IN_VITRO for the accelerated fibril formation and cross-seeding it asserts, which the paper measured on recombinant protein; the steric zipper motif itself was identified by a structure-based threading prediction in the same study.

steps/6.description: The disease variants in HNRNPA2B1 and HNRNPA1 lie in the glycine-rich prion-like domain that both paralogues carry. Wild-type hnRNPA2 and hnRNPA1 already have an intrinsic tendency to self-assemble into fibrils; the variants strengthen a steric zipper motif inside that domain, which accelerates formation of self-seeding fibrils and lets them cross-seed polymerization of the wild-type protein. The proximal defect in the hnRNP forms of this disorder is therefore a gain of ordered self-assembly, not the loss of ubiquitin dependent segregase activity that drives the VCP form.

evidence.snippet: Notably, the disease mutations promote excess incorporation of hnRNPA2 and hnRNPA1 into stress granules and drive the formation of cytoplasmic inclusions in animal models that recapitulate the human pathology.
evidence.explanation: Supports both the excess stress-granule incorporation and the cytoplasmic inclusion formation this node asserts. Graded MODEL_ORGANISM because the quoted sentence attributes the inclusion phenotype to animal models.

evidence.snippet: analysis of muscle tissue from patient II5 (family 1) showed that hnRNPA2B1 cleared from many nuclei and accumulated in cytoplasmic inclusions in ~10% of fibers
evidence.explanation: The human counterpart of the model finding, quantifying nuclear clearance and cytoplasmic accumulation in patient muscle.

steps/7.description: Mutant hnRNPA2 and hnRNPA1 are incorporated in excess into stress granules and form cytoplasmic inclusions. In the two reported families the corresponding human pathology is nuclear clearance of the affected hnRNP with cytoplasmic accumulation in a minority of muscle fibers, alongside TDP-43 pathology of the same kind seen in the VCP form and in sporadic inclusion body myositis. This is the point at which the hnRNP arm and the VCP arm of the disorder converge on a shared aggregate pathology.

evidence.snippet: a defining feature of IBMPFD-related myopathy is the accumulation of large, ubiquitin-positive “rimmed vacuoles”
evidence.explanation: This paper links IBMPFD myopathy to rimmed-vacuole pathology.

evidence.snippet: Approximately 90% of the affected persons in the study have myopathy or muscle weakness particularly of the shoulder and hip girdles
evidence.explanation: Human clinical review identifies myopathy and limb-girdle weakness as the dominant disease manifestation.

steps/8.description: Skeletal muscle fibers develop a vacuolar inclusion-body pathology with rimmed vacuoles, elevated creatine kinase, myopathic EMG abnormalities, and progressive proximal and distal weakness.

evidence.snippet: Paget disease of bone characterized by abnormal rates of bone growth that can result in bone pain, enlargement and fractures.
evidence.explanation: Human clinical review supports the abnormal bone-remodeling branch.

steps/9.description: The bone branch of IBMPFD manifests as Paget disease, with abnormal rates of bone growth, osteolysis, elevated alkaline phosphatase, pain, enlargement, and fracture susceptibility.

evidence.snippet: Findings of premature FTD affecting behavior and personality are seen in a third of affected individuals.
evidence.explanation: Human clinical review supports frontotemporal neurodegeneration as part of the triad.

steps/10.description: Premature frontotemporal degeneration produces behavioral, personality, and language-predominant cognitive decline with cerebral inclusion bodies and brain atrophy in a subset of affected individuals.

evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists waddling gait as very frequent.

evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists ubiquitin-positive cerebral inclusion bodies as very frequent.

evidence.explanation: Source for the lumping decision stated in this row, and the reason ClinGen's HNRNPA2B1 assertion is keyed on the IBMPFD2 class rather than on amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

evidence.snippet: The disease entity oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy 2 (MONDO:0958195) has been split from this curation for difference in phenotype (especially ptosis and eye movement paralysis) and a distinct difference in molecular mechanism (frameshift variants that create the same novel amino acid series at the C-terminus of the protein).
evidence.explanation: Source for the split stated in this row, and the reason the HNRNPA2B1 oculopharyngeal phenotype is not covered by this entry.
